title: Over a henselian pair, $V(\mathfrak p+I)$ is connected
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and $\mathfrak p\subseteq A$ a prime ideal. Then the closed subset $V(\mathfrak p+I)=\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}A:\mathfrak q\supseteq\mathfrak p+I\}$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] in the subspace topology (in particular nonempty).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.11.16 (Tag 09Y6, label lemma-irreducible-henselian-pair-connected, line 2948); 'connected' includes nonempty (Topology, Definition 5.7.1)

proof.text: The quotient A/p is a nonzero domain since p is prime. Apply henselianRing_of_isIntegral to obtain the henselian pair (A/p,I.map(algebraMap A (A/p))).
Apply PrimeSpectrum.connectedSpace_zeroLocus_of_henselian_domain to the extended ideal. This proves connectedness and nonemptiness of its zero locus.

Take the continuous image under PrimeSpectrum.comap of Ideal.Quotient.mk p. Mathlib image_comap_zeroLocus_eq_zeroLocus_comap identifies it with V(comap(map I)), and Ideal.comap_map_of_surjective together with Ideal.mk_ker gives comap(map I)=I ⊔ p. Transport IsConnected to ConnectedSpace of V(p ⊔ I). The full scheme closed-immersion theorem is unnecessary.

split_report.summary: Split the Stacks 09Y6 proof into quotient reduction, a direct proof that the quotient is nonzero from the henselian lifting condition, and the nontrivial-idempotent contradiction in a domain. The quotient-spectrum homeomorphism is made explicit using the existing quotient closed-immersion Mathlib leaf and affine-spectrum definition; the affine clopen-idempotent correspondence supplies the contradiction. No new nodes were needed, and the item already had the required three Mathlib searches.

Three steps, no new nodes, following 09Y6: reduction to the domain A/p with the henselian pair (A/p,(I+p)/p) by lem-weil-pbc-integral-over-henselian-pair and the closed-immersion identification of Spec of the quotient with V(p+I); A/I nonzero because the zero quotient would have the two idempotent lifts 0 and 1 in the domain A; a disconnection of Spec(A/I) would give a nontrivial idempotent of A/I (lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent), which lifts to an idempotent of the domain A, hence to 0 or 1, contradiction. The review by C1 is a real review.
